title: Finite families of triangle denominators admit common refinements and equalizers
statement: Let $S$ be a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the triangulated category [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], and fix a distinguished triangle $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ in the pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $\mathcal I$ be the category whose objects are morphisms of distinguished triangles $(s,s',s''):(X',Y',Z',f',g',h')\to(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ with all three components in $S$, and whose arrows are commuting morphisms of the source triangles with all three components in $S$. Given finitely many objects of $\mathcal I$, there is another object of $\mathcal I$ with an arrow from it to each of them. Given two parallel arrows in $\mathcal I$, there is an object of $\mathcal I$ and an arrow to their common source after which the two composites agree componentwise.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 05R9 (lemma-limit-triangles), cofilteredness/equalization construction

proof.text: Let T_1 and T_2 be denominator triangles over T=(X,Y,Z). The category S/X is cofiltered by [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], so their X-denominators have a common predecessor X_3. Every arrow p:X_3\to X_1 of S/X lies in S: with u=s_{1,X}\circ p in S, the second MS2 clause applied to u and s_{1,X} gives t in S and q with s_{1,X}\circ t=u\circ q=s_{1,X}\circ p\circ q, the second MS3 clause gives t' in S with t\circ t'=p\circ q\circ t', so p\circ(q\circ t') is in S by MS1, and MS4 applied to s_{1,X},p,q\circ t' gives p in S; the same holds for X_3\to X_2 and, after rotation, for the Y- and Z-component maps into T_1 and T_2, so the final a,b,c lie in S. Complete the S-arrow X_3\to X_1 to a denominator triangle morphism by [lem-pur-triangle-completion-ms6-05r9]. Repeating this after rotation for Y and Z gives a predecessor triangle with component maps a,b,c into T_2, but these maps need not commute with its triangle arrows. For the f-square, compose the two candidates f_2 a and b f_1 with the Y-component s_{2,Y}:Y_2\to Y of T_2\to T. They agree because both become f s_{2,X}a=f s_{1,X} on composing the component maps to T. The second MS3 clause therefore gives an S-denominator into their common source on which the f-square commutes. Complete that denominator to a triangle map by [lem-pur-triangle-completion-ms6-05r9]. Rotate and repeat for the g- and h-squares; earlier equalities persist on precomposition. The final a,b,c form a triangle morphism, yielding a common predecessor of T_1 and T_2. Iterate binary predecessors for a finite nonempty family; for the empty family take the identity triangle, using MS1.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 05R9 (lemma-limit-triangles), cofilteredness construction for finitely many objects

proof.text: Let (a,b,c) and (a',b',c') be parallel arrows T_1\to T_2 in I, and write s_1:T_1\to T for the denominator triangle map. Their equality after composition with s_1 gives s_{2,X}a=s_{2,X}a' on X-components, where s_{2,X} is the X-component of T_2\to T. The second MS3 clause supplies t_X in S into X_1 with at_X=a't_X. Complete t_X to a denominator triangle morphism T_3\to T_1 by [lem-pur-triangle-completion-ms6-05r9]; the X-components of the parallel composites now agree. Rotate the triangles and repeat the same argument for b,b', then for c,c'. Each replacement precomposes all components, so previously obtained equalities persist, while MS1 keeps composite components in S. The final composite T_5\to T_1 equalizes the original parallel arrows componentwise.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 05R9 (lemma-limit-triangles), equalization of parallel arrows

proof.text: The finite-family refinement and the equalization construction use only arrows in S and commuting morphisms of distinguished triangles, so they are objects and arrows of the stated category I. These are exactly the two cofilteredness conditions: every finite pair has a common predecessor, and every parallel pair is equalized after precomposition.
